answer: Cross-Held Capability Ledger. Each identity must hold a unique capability set issued by a distinct bridge peer, and any two identities sharing a capability key are auto-flagged. Registration demands solving a per-key opal challenge tied to that peer’s ledger slice. Attackers duplicating an identity must either acquire new timber-backed issuance slots, each costing a full peer audit plus fresh challenge computation, or link keys and expose the cluster. Per-duplicate cost: one audit cycle and one replayable challenge proof.
